title: Petra and the Regiment
premise: In a river town on the edge of an empire's collapse, Beatrix Halloran must complete the master atlas her dead mentor died protecting — the only map that proves where a massacred regiment was truly sent, and by whose order. When a mute child is abandoned at the workshop door carrying half of a soldier's dispatch case, Beatrix realizes the girl is the last living witness to that massacre, and that the men who ordered it have come to erase her. As the river ice thaws and the workshop's protection with it, Beatrix races to engrave the truth into copper plates while sheltering the child, falling in love with the deserter officer sent to kill them both who instead chooses memory over orders. The atlas is finished and smuggled out as the workshop burns; justice comes not from any court but from ten thousand printed copies, and Beatrix leaves town with the child and the man, trading a life of careful silences for one dangerous testimony.
about_author: Noor Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military survey records before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about the people history forgot to name, and lives near a cold river she refuses to swim in.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Five years after Master Aldous Halloran's death, she inks the final coastlines of his atlas alone in the winter-locked workshop, hiding her authorship behind his name. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into discipline, and the first crack in it when she admits she cannot remember his face clearly.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Ice
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A child of about seven appears at the door at dawn, frostbitten, clutching half a leather dispatch case, with a note: forget the face. Beatrix breaks her own rule of silence and takes her in. Emotional beat: fear warring with a conscience she has kept caged for five years.

chapters.title: What the Case Contains
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Inside the case: a torn regimental route order bearing Aldous's annotations — proof the Ninth were marched somewhere the official record says they never went. The child draws the rest of the route from memory. Emotional beat: the atlas stops being a memorial and becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Cartographer
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Elias Vane's POV. A disgraced officer arrives in town under civilian cover, ordered to locate a missing dispatch case and 'the loose end' attached to it. He visits the workshop posing as a buyer. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to fray at the sight of ink-stained hands and a guarded woman.

chapters.title: Silences That Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She teaches the child, whom she names Petra, the workshop's rules of invisibility while interrogating her gently through drawings. Petra's sketches reveal she watched soldiers die. Emotional beat: tenderness growing inside dread.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confirms the case came off the ice upstream and traces it to the workshop, but delays reporting, walking the frozen river at night and reading Aldous's old survey marks. Emotional beat: duty and doubt pulling in opposite directions for the first time.

chapters.title: Copper and Memory
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She begins secretly engraving the true route onto a hidden plate beneath the atlas's decorative border, working only by candlelight. Petra helps grind ink, becoming her accomplice. Emotional beat: purpose replacing fear — the work itself as resistance.

chapters.title: An Honest Lie
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Under direct questioning from his handler, Colonel Merrick's agent, Elias lies about the case's location — his first act of treason. He returns to the workshop to warn Beatrix without explaining why he can be trusted. Emotional beat: the point of no return crossed quietly.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Maps
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Beatrix and Elias circle each other across a drafting table, each concealing what they know, until she catches him studying the false drawer. Emotional beat: suspicion sharpening into intimacy — two liars recognizing the same craft.

chapters.title: Petra Speaks
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Petra breaks her muteness at night, naming the village where the Ninth were marched and describing the colonel's voice. Beatrix realizes the child is the massacre's only witness and the reason the plates matter. Emotional beat: heartbreak and resolve fused.

chapters.title: The Thaw Begins
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The river ice groans; supply boats and soldiers will follow within weeks. Merrick's men arrive early and search neighboring buildings. Elias burns his own reports to buy time. Emotional beat: the clock becoming audible in every scene.

chapters.title: What Aldous Died For
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In Aldous's hidden correspondence she finds he had corresponded with a widow of the Ninth — and that his death was ruled accidental two days after he refused to falsify the route. Emotional beat: rage, and the understanding that she inherited more than an atlas.

chapters.title: The Buyer from the Capital
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Merrick himself arrives, charming and patient, commissioning a copy of the atlas as pretext to inspect the workshop. Elias must stand in the room while the man who wrote the massacre order praises Aldous's craft. Emotional beat: controlled nausea; love hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: Hidden Plate, Open Hand
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She confesses everything to Elias — the plate, the route, Petra — and asks him to choose. He gives her Merrick's travel schedule instead of arresting her. Emotional beat: trust offered like a blade hilt-first, and accepted.

chapters.title: Proofs and Pursuit
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. First proof sheets are pulled; Merrick's agents find the widow's letters missing and close the net. Beatrix sends Petra to the printer's widow for safekeeping, and the child refuses to let go of her hand. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: The Night the Presses Turned
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. In the printer's cellar, three hundred copies run overnight while soldiers patrol above. Elias holds the door against a suspicious sergeant with nothing but paperwork and nerve. Emotional beat: terror and triumph in the same hour.

chapters.title: Merrick's Offer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Merrick confronts Beatrix privately: finish the atlas under his name, hand over the child, and live comfortably. She answers with the master's old phrase about maps that tell the truth. Emotional beat: quiet defiance at gunpoint; love declared by what she refuses.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The workshop is set alight to destroy the evidence; Beatrix and Elias rescue the hidden plate through the coal chute as the roof falls, Elias wounded. Emotional beat: loss of the past made physical — five years of safety burning.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The printed atlases reach garrison towns, newspapers, and Parliament's rivals; officers of the Ninth's survivors demand inquiry. Merrick's patronage collapses faster than any trial could. Emotional beat: vindication arriving sideways, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: The Face Worth Remembering
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, the chapter's only child's-eye view. Petra describes the fire, the escape, and choosing to remember the faces she was told to forget — including Beatrix's. Emotional beat: healing; memory reclaimed as inheritance rather than wound.

chapters.title: Where the River Breaks
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Merrick, exposed, chooses the river rather than the gallows; Elias testifies anyway, ending his career to make the record whole. He and Beatrix part from the army formally and from each other not at all. Emotional beat: duty fulfilled by betrayal of the wrong master.

chapters.title: The Atlas Under New Hands
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In a new riverside workshop, Beatrix signs the corrected atlas with both names — Aldous's and her own — while Petra learns lettering and Elias mends the press. The ice breaks cleanly at last. Emotional beat: home rebuilt around truth instead of silence.
